newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Wall St slide erodes Euro share gains.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Wall St slide erodes Euro share gains.

text.p: A steep early slide on Wall Street dragged European equities from the record levels they hit on Wednesday morning when they were spurred by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's comments on the U.S. economy.
Wall Street's Dow Jones industrial average was down almost 70 points at 1500 gmt following a sharp drop in the shares of International Business Machines Corp.
IBM was down $13-1/4 at $156-1/8 on Wednesday after reporting fourth quarter earnings on Tuesday which beat the First Call consenus estimate but disappointed many analysts.
The dollar also retreated a touch from its earlier gains when it surged to levels against the yen and mark not seen for several years.
Gold, which earlier tumbled below $350 an ounce for the first time since late 1993, rallied a touch to fix at $351.20 in the afternoon however.

Earlier, European markets focused just as much on what Greenspan did not say in his testimony to the U.S. Senate on Tuesday as what he did say. Only last month he wiped billions off share values by warning of "irrational exuberance".
"Greenspan's speech seems to have been taken very well and he didn't take the chance to knock Wall Street down to earth," said one London dealer said.
Investors had feared that Greenspan would repeat his warning that world markets were overheating, which sent stock markets reeling across the globe last month.

Since then investors have regained their courage and the Dow Jones Industrial average has risen about 400 points. But this time Greenspan, the epitome of the prudent central banker, on Tuesday described the stock markets' performance only as breathtaking.
That was all the markets needed. The Dow closed up 40.03 points at a record 6,883.90 on Tuesday and European markets followed suit on Wednesday.
All leading European markets moved into record territory during the morning, though by 1500 GMT they were well off their best levels after Wall Street's slide.
In London, the FTSE 100 index was up just 9.4 points at 4,204.9 and in Paris the CAC-40 index up 0.96 percent at 2433.08 points, having been up by more than 1.5 percent earlier.

In Frankfurt the Ibis Dax index of post-bourse dealing was up 14.07 at 3014.73. Earlier, Wall Street and the buoyant dollar, which helps German exporters, pushed the main DAX index up two percent to a record high before easing slightly.
The dollar edged back after storming through 1.64 marks during the morning to a 31-month high and flirting with 119 yen, a level last seen 46 months ago.
Greenspan gave the impetus, with investors noting his comment that tight U.S. labour markets had not stoked inflation. At midmorning it was at 1.6409 marks and 118.85.

Outside the U.S., an Italian interest rate cut and a weak German business climate survey on Tuesday buoyed the dollar as they pointed to lower rates in Europe, analysts said. "It's all coming together. People have set in their minds clear targets of the mid-1.60s against the mark...and 120 to 125 against the yen," said Stephen Hannah, director of research at IBJ International in London.
Gold slipped below $350 an ounce for the first time since October 1993 to $349.70 during the morning from $353.65 at Tuesday's London close, though it rallied during the afternoon.
"People have been trying to force it lower this morning. It's looking very dodgy," one London-based dealer said.

Bullion has been sliding steadily since a high of $417 last February, with investors ignoring gold in favour of the surging stock markets. The decline has gathered steam this month amid fears of central bank sales.
CURRENCIES AT 1500 GMT
The dollar stood at 118.70 yen and 1.6380 marks from Tuesday's late European levels of 117.78 and 1.6240.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1500 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was up 9.4 points at 4,204.9.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was 23.20 points higher at 2,433.08.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 51.96 points at 3,028.68, though the Ibis Dax index of post-bourse trading was up just 14.07 at 3,014.73.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1500 GMT
Gold fixed at $351.20 in the afternoon after falling to $349.70 in the morning from a $353.65 close in London on Tuesday.
